heading: Whether the Native shall obtaine his Wife with ease, or much difficulty

groups.topic: Printed CXXXI header and easy/difficult spouse acquisition

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP CXXXI Whether Native shall obtaine his Wife with ease or difficulty
claims.historical_meaning: This separate numbered source concerns obstacles in obtaining a wife, distinct from whether marriage happens at all.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: greater part of Significators fortunate Planets
claims.historical_meaning: A majority of favorable marriage indicators supports the author's easy-relationship-access claim.
Well-fortified indicators provide a second favorable alternative, not necessarily requiring benefic nature.
Lilly asserts ease of obtaining marriage under favorable majority, without independent observed marriages.
Weak marriage indicators form a contrasting condition to fortunate ones.
The unfavorable planetary indicators are also named, not simply weakness alone.
The author alleges greater difficulty obtaining a wife under weakened adverse testimony.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: if they all be imbecill and ill affected
claims.historical_meaning: A stronger negative branch requires all rather than only the majority of indicia ill affected.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: make love unto many and as oft deluded
claims.historical_meaning: A separate alleged outcome is repeated unsuccessful romantic pursuit, not necessarily lack of marriage.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: much difficulty in procuring a Wife
claims.historical_meaning: The author asserts a prolonged difficult pursuit under the all-weak combination.

groups.topic: Venus-Mars aspect, benefic/malefic strength and normative happiness

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Venus not in some good aspect with Mars
claims.historical_meaning: Absence of a favorable Venus-Mars aspect is offered as an additional relationship-difficulty allegation.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: suffer many inconveniences in his loves or affections
claims.historical_meaning: Lilly assigns relationship inconvenience from the absence of Venus-Mars benefit, without reliable measured effects.
Positive planetary types are alleged to make obtaining marriage happy, distinct from ease/difficulty alone.
The author scales alleged happiness by benefic strength without a calibrated outcome or time horizon.
Malefic indicators are said to imply effort even when powerful, a separate power-versus-benefit distinction.
Powerful malefics are expressly not treated as equivalent to beneficial planets for marriage happiness.

groups.topic: Author's retrospective difficult-to-marry anecdotes and historical sexual stereotypes

claims.historical_meaning: Lilly invokes unaudited retrospective personal observations, not denominated prospective evidence.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Saturn and Mars in Opposition out of first and seventh houses
claims.historical_meaning: A Saturn/Mars opposing first-vs-seventh configuration is alleged as one difficult marriage case; verify exact planetary glyph independently.
Saturn close to the seventh cusp is proposed as a second independent alternative difficulty source.
These two signs for Venus form a third purported source of difficulty, without valid comparative outcomes.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Venus not in aspect of Mars
claims.historical_meaning: The Venus Leo/Scorpio case additionally requires missing aspect to Mars.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Mars Virgo Capricorn or Taurus in seventh
claims.historical_meaning: The source alleges a fourth alternate difficulty source from Mars in seventh and listed signs.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: whether in aspect Venus or not
claims.historical_meaning: The Mars-seventh branch explicitly allows Venus contact or none, increasing scope/flexibility.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: married at last upon a sudden
claims.historical_meaning: Lilly says such a person may nevertheless marry abruptly, a counterexample to permanent bachelorhood.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: extraordinary difficulty to procure a Wife
claims.historical_meaning: The author groups those four paths as evidence of great obstacles rather than permanent no marriage.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: prone to Women and abounded in Lasciviousnesse
claims.historical_meaning: The historical vignette ascribes an individual's sexual conduct/morality without independent evidence.

groups.topic: Time of Marriage: east Sun orientation and corresponding houses

claims.historical_meaning: An unnumbered smaller heading inside CXXXI shifts from difficulty to timing, not to a new chapter.
The early-age source branch starts with majority agreement, not an isolated Moon placement.
Moon relative to Sun's oriental status is an additional qualifier for the early/mature-spouse-age contrast.
The relevant signifiers must be placed in source-defined oriental house sectors.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: tenth eleventh twelfth fourth fifth sixth
claims.historical_meaning: Lilly names six houses as eastern quadrants in this particular timing rubric.
The author alleges an early marriage under the oriental condition without defining youth age in years.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: after more mature years espouse a young Woman
claims.historical_meaning: A late marriage to a younger partner is explicitly given as an OR alternative to marriage young.

groups.topic: Occidental sources and west house list; age and partner-widow alternative

claims.historical_meaning: The source contrasts occidental marriage indicators with the preceding oriental Moon-source case.
The alleged later-marriage rubric also requires a matching quarter of the natal chart.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: ninth eighth seventh first second third
claims.historical_meaning: These six houses are explicitly listed as occidental quarters; do not infer modern quadrant convention.
One alleged result is a late wedding, without date or age threshold.
An alternative result permits early marriage if the spouse is previously married, not late marriage in all cases.
Another alternative result is youth marriage to much older spouse, mixing partner age with event age.

groups.topic: Direct/swift and retrograde/slow/stationary motion; discordant source priority

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: observe the motion of the Significators
claims.historical_meaning: Lilly adds planetary movement status as a timing diagnostic distinct from solar oriental/occidental placement.
Direct motion of the relevant indicators is the first qualifier in alleged early marriage.
Swiftness is an additional requirement of the early-case directional claim.
The author associates direct and swift indicators with early marriage, not a quantified calendar date.
Retrogradation is one separate alleged delay source.
Slow planetary motion is a second separate alleged delay source.
Stationarity provides a third alleged delay alternative.
No number of months/years is provided for this alleged delay.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: if then you find a discrepancy
claims.historical_meaning: Conflicting natal testimonies are explicitly considered, contradicting a one-planet certainty framework.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: respect Significators nearest agree with Moon or Venus especially Moon
claims.historical_meaning: The source proposes weighting consistency with Moon most, but leaves closeness/weights undefined.

groups.topic: Historical specific primary directions: seventh degree/lord or Moon/Venus to Ascendant degree/lord

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: more special time best adjudged from directions
claims.historical_meaning: Lilly transitions from qualitative signifier motion to directions as proposed event timing.
Seventh cusp degree is the first possible directed source object.
Seventh ruler is another direction source alternative.
Moon is named independently as a possible source of direction.
Venus is also an independent source object.
Ascendant cusp degree is one specified target of directions.
Ascendant ruler is an alternative target of the directions.
No directional arc-to-year/calendar conversion is actually supplied in the paragraph.

groups.topic: Lilly's preferred Midheaven directions to Venus or Moon and radix dignity

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: my judgement ... opinions of Ancients contrary
claims.historical_meaning: The author explicitly identifies his preference as differing from previous astrologers, not an independent validation.
Midheaven is a proposed promissor or directed point in Lilly's claimed marriage-timing method.
Conjunction/contact with Venus is an eligible MC direction endpoint.
MC to Venus sextile is one proposed aspect direction.
MC to Venus square is another accepted direction, even though it is traditionally adverse.
MC to Venus trine is another allowed source direction.
Lilly limits the preferred Venus aspect timing route to a strong natal Venus.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: or to same aspects with Moon
claims.historical_meaning: Moon can substitute as another aspect target for MC directions.

groups.topic: Sun direct and converse directions; Moon to Sun or Mars with adverse-aspect bounds caveat

claims.historical_meaning: Sun direct direction is named as one marriage-timing source.
The source also admits converse directions; exact geometry must be separately established.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: to Body of Moon or Venus
claims.historical_meaning: Direct/converse Sun to Moon/Venus conjunction is an eligible event aspect.
Seventh marriage timing instructions include Sun directed to a sextile with Moon/Venus.
The author also includes adverse square aspects in claimed marriage timing.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: or Trine of Moon or Venus
claims.historical_meaning: The trine is another endpoint condition in that solar direction group.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: direction of Moon to premised aspects to Sun
claims.historical_meaning: Moon can be directed toward eligible aspects with Sun.
The author also includes Moon directions to Mars, potentially contradicting malefic-only pessimism.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: if direction meet Square or Opposition Sun or Mars
claims.historical_meaning: The author gives an additional caveat specifically for harder directed aspects to Sun/Mars.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: see if fall not in Terms of a Fortune
claims.historical_meaning: Historical benefic planetary bounds/terms are used as a qualifier; exact bounds/epoch not transcribed.

groups.topic: Alternative Midheaven, Sun or Moon favorable aspects to seventh ruler or occupant

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: mid-heaven directed to Sextile or Trine
claims.historical_meaning: The Midheaven can be directed to favorable aspects with marriage indicators.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: or Sun directed to Sextile or Trine
claims.historical_meaning: Solar directions to positive marriage configurations form another eligible source.

claims.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: or Moon directed to Sextile or Trine
claims.historical_meaning: Lunar directions to the same favorable contacts form another source.
Seventh-house ruler is an eligible destination for these beneficial aspects.
A benefic planet occupying seventh is another eligible timing target.
The author associates these varied directions with marriage timing, without a chart-to-date worked example.
